title: Make the shop's tariffs right whichever page is opened first

blocks.text: The subscription shop has two ways in. Most visitors open the price list first; some go straight to the sign-up form. After a restart last week, the first visitor went straight to sign-up, and every customer who signed up until the next restart was billed without VAT. In the staging environment, where the price list is usually opened first, the sign-up form failed instead: new customers had no tariff at all.
`Tariff` and its `STANDARD` tariff are fine as they are. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Pricing.java`, both in `Rates`:

items: `vatPercent()`: the VAT configured for this deployment (`configuredVat()` reads it);
`defaultTariff()`: the tariff a new customer starts on, which is the standard tariff.

blocks.text: When you're done, the standard tariff charges the configured VAT and every new customer starts on it, whichever of the two the shop uses first after a start. About three lines in total.
Each test starts the shop afresh: it loads its own copy of the `Pricing` classes, so their static fields are set up again, in the order that test uses them.

cases.says: the VAT the shop reports is the one configured for the deployment
when the standard tariff is the first thing used, it charges the configured VAT
when the default tariff is the first thing used, it still charges the configured VAT
when the standard tariff was used first, the default tariff asked for afterwards is that standard tariff

origin.section: Static Initialisers Run in Textual Order, and a Cycle Lets Code Read a Field Before It Is Set

concepts: Static initialisers run in textual order, and in a cycle between two classes the class used second reads the first one's field before it is set, so a final field keeps a default value that depends on which class was used first.
